title: REST Resources & HTTP Verbs Made Clear

scenes.line1: Why do REST APIs use verbs?
scenes.say: Why do REST APIs use HTTP verbs, and why should you care in an interview?

scenes.label: Resource
scenes.sub: A resource is a thing, like a user or order.
scenes.say: In REST, a resource is just an object—think user or order—exposed by your API.
You act on resources with HTTP verbs. GET reads, POST creates, PUT replaces, DELETE removes. Only POST is not idempotent.
Idempotency means repeating the same request gives the same result. GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent. POST is not.

scenes.question: Which verb is NOT idempotent?
scenes.right: POST is not idempotent. It can create new resources each time.
scenes.say: Watch out—only POST is not idempotent. PUT and DELETE are safe to repeat.
